description: A new command for an existing std-only Python CLI, dockctl (a city bike-share's ops tool with list and show commands, a gateway client built on urllib with no timeouts, a fake gateway for its tests, and docs/gateway-api.md, which says each client may have at most 16 requests in progress and gets 429 beyond that, and that the gateway waits up to 60 seconds on a dock that does not answer). The ticket asks for `dockctl sweep`: every dock's status (about 200), one line per dock in ID order as `show` prints it, offline docks (no answer within 2 seconds) and failed ones (an HTTP error) reported in stated forms, a summary line, exit 0/1/2, inside a 20-second health check, within the gateway's documented limits. It names no technique. A sequential sweep is correct and takes over 40 seconds. One that starts every read at once, or sizes its pool from the CPU count, is refused past 16. One that gives up on a read without closing its connection (wait_for around a blocking read, a thread joined with a timeout), or only paces its reads, goes over 16 in the outage case, where more docks are offline than the limit, whatever its own cap. One that keeps a silent dock's request open after giving up on it (a fixed pool whose worker stays blocked on the read while the sweep moves on) stays within 16 and exits on time on an ordinary day, but holds each such request for the gateway's 60 seconds, so in the outage the whole sweep waits on them. Every case runs in its own bubblewrap sandbox with a hidden gateway inside its network namespace (hidden/driver.py; datasets and expected reports made in check.py and passed on standard input), with PYTHON_CPU_COUNT=32 and on more than 16 CPUs (the run is invalid otherwise), so a pool sized from the CPU count is judged alike on every host that decides: a main case (203 docks, some slow but within 2 s, some answering only after 3 to 6 s, some offline, some failing), an all-answering case (40), an outage (203 docks, 20 offline and 30 slow, all in the first third of both orders), no gateway, and list/show against a small gateway. Required: answered_docks_correct (every answering dock's line, ID order, in the main, all-answering, and outage cases), failures_handled (offline and failed lines, summary, exit 1 and 0, exit 2 within 10 s with no gateway), within_budget (the main case exits within max(20 s, 5x the best of up to three runs of a correct reference client timed in the same check), having asked for every dock, and the outage within 5x the reference's time on it; the run is invalid when 5x the reference reaches the sequential floor; the main and all-answering cases are killed only at twice that floor, so a slow but correct sweep fails this check alone), within_limit (the gateway refused nothing in any case; at least one dock asked), no_held_requests (no request in progress at the gateway longer than 8 s while the command ran, in any case; at least one dock asked), no_work_after_exit (nothing reaches the gateway in the 2 s after exit, no process left), existing_commands_unchanged (list and show as the fixture's tests expect, run as commands). Measures: seconds, peak and attempted requests in progress, refusals, abandoned and held requests, the longest time a request stayed in progress (the reference client's too), requests in progress at exit, mean requests in progress, requests per dock, the CPUs and CPU count the command saw, the fixture's tests against the agent's package, the agent's own suite. Needs bubblewrap, python3 3.10 or later (3.13 or later for the CPU count to be fixed), and more than 16 CPUs; agent arms need nothing extra readable.
prompt: Ops wants a `dockctl sweep` command for the uptime monitor. It should read every dock (about 200 of them now) and print one line per dock in dock-ID order, the same line `dockctl show` prints, then a last line like `swept 187 docks: 180 ok, 5 offline, 2 failed`. A few docks are always offline (dead modems) and the gateway just sits on those, so a dock that hasn't answered within 2 seconds should come out as `D-0123: offline`; when the gateway answers with an error, print `D-0123: failed (HTTP 502)` with its status code. Exit 0 if every dock was read, 1 if any was offline or failed, and 2 if we can't get the dock list at all. The monitor's health check gives a command 20 seconds. And please stay within the gateway's limits in docs/gateway-api.md; we had our access blocked for an afternoon last month.
